summary.prose: A four-task build: the decision-table unit tests first (red), then the reclaim itself in the EEXIST branch of the shared acquireRunFileGuard, then consumer-path integration cases with real exited-process fixtures, then the full sweep confirming the untouched consumers keep their contracts. All code change lives in one module; every consumer inherits the recovery for free.

tasks.summary: Test-first: extend src/shared/__tests__/daemon-run-files.test.ts with the decision-table cases - gone -> quarantine+acquire, previous-boot replaced -> quarantine+acquire, same/same-boot-replaced/corrupt-or-missing owner.json/throwing reader -> withhold with nothing renamed, retry EEXIST -> recompute and throw, symlink -> conflict, quarantine-name collision -> suffixed name, daemonLog line by nonce, log-write failure swallowed. Uses mkdtemp guard fixtures and a fake ProcessIdentityReader injected via the new optional third parameter.

tasks.summary: Implement the reclaim in the EEXIST branch of acquireRunFileGuard (src/shared/daemon-run-files.ts): add the optional ProcessIdentityReader third param, read ownerRecord, compute processIdentityState plus the boot-id comparison ('gone', or recorded boot segment differs from the current boot), rename the stale guard to '<path>.quarantine-<UTC-timestamp>-<recorded-nonce>' with incremented-suffix collision handling, append a best-effort recovery line to PATHS.daemonLog (failures swallowed), retry mkdirSync once and recompute the conflict on retry EEXIST. Add renameSync/appendFileSync to the fs import; narrow the comments at :51 and :73 to the unverifiable-owner case.
